context.content:
Billing Core turns usage and subscriptions into invoices and collects payment.
It is a Python 3.11 FastAPI service. It is the only service allowed to talk to
the payment provider; every other service asks Billing Core instead of calling
the provider directly.

context.content:

context.heading: Vocabulary
context.content:

artefact. A *delivery* is one attempt to hand a document to a recipient through

context.content:

context.content:

  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.acme.dev/avatars/ada.png",
  "locale": "en-GB",

question: Il provider non viene mai chiamato. Perché?

context.heading: Authorisation errors
context.content:
`insufficient_scope` (HTTP 403) is returned when a route requires a scope the
token does not carry, for example calling `GET /users/:id` without
`users:read`.

context.heading: POST /webhooks/stripe
context.content:
Receives Stripe callbacks. The route verifies the Stripe signature header
before doing anything else, stores the raw event in `webhook_events` and returns
HTTP 200 immediately. Processing happens asynchronously in `billing-worker`.

context.heading: A provider was never called
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` rejects a delivery before calling any provider when the channel
has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: Runtime
context.content:
The service runs as a stateless container. Two replicas are deployed per
environment. Sessions are not held in memory: every request is authenticated
from the bearer token, so any replica can serve any request.

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

answer:
La causa documentata è il routing del canale.

`ProviderRouter` rifiuta la delivery prima di chiamare qualsiasi provider quando il canale non ha una mappatura in `docsync.channels`; in quel caso la delivery viene registrata con `unsupported_channel` e non è presente nessun `provider_message_id` [08-troubleshooting.md — A provider was never called].

Coerentemente, se il canale non ha mappatura la delivery viene rifiutata subito con `unsupported_channel` e nessun provider viene chiamato [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter]. La mappatura è `docsync.channels`, che associa un nome di canale a un bean provider, ad esempio `email: emailDeliveryProvider`; un canale assente dalla mappa è non supportato a runtime [06-configuration.md — Channel routing].

Da verificare: il valore del campo `channel` della richiesta e la presenza della chiave corrispondente in `docsync.channels`. La tabella di routing è costruita all'avvio dalla configurazione, quindi una modifica non applicata a runtime è un'ipotesi coerente ma non confermata dalle sezioni fornite [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter].

question: Come funziona GET /me?

context.heading: Current User Flow
context.content:
1. The client calls `GET /me` with a bearer token.
2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

If the profile row is missing, step 5 returns the default profile, so
`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: GET /me
context.content:
Returns the authenticated user. The route requires a valid bearer token and is
handled by `UserController.getMe`, which calls `UserService.getCurrentUser`.
The response body is:

```json
{
  "id": "uuid",
  "email": "user@example.com",
  "displayName": "Ada Lovelace",
  "avatarUrl": "https://cdn.acme.dev/avatars/ada.png",
  "locale": "en-GB",
  "status": "active"
}
```

`displayName`, `avatarUrl` and `locale` come from the profile record. `id`,
`email` and `status` come from the account record.

answer:
`GET /me` restituisce l'utente autenticato e richiede un bearer token valido.

Percorso documentato:
- `authMiddleware` verifica il token e imposta `req.auth.userId` [05-main-flows.md — Current User Flow]
- `UserController.getMe` chiama `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)` [04-api-reference.md — GET /me]
- `UserService` carica l'account con `UserRepository.findById` e i campi di profilo con `ProfileService.getProfile`, poi unisce i due record in `CurrentUser` [05-main-flows.md — Current User Flow]

Nel payload `id`, `email` e `status` provengono dal record account, mentre `displayName`, `avatarUrl` e `locale` provengono dal record di profilo [04-api-reference.md — GET /me].

question: Come funziona la firma dei documenti?

context.heading: Document production flow
context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
Billing Core turns usage and subscriptions into invoices and collects payment.
It is a Python 3.11 FastAPI service. It is the only service allowed to talk to
the payment provider; every other service asks Billing Core instead of calling
the provider directly.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

context.heading: webhook_events
context.content:
`webhook_events` stores every received Stripe event with `provider_event_id`
(unique), `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`. The unique index on
`provider_event_id` is what makes webhook processing idempotent.

context.heading: SignatureService
context.content:
`SignatureService` applies a PAdES seal using the certificate loaded from the
HSM at startup. If the certificate cannot be loaded the application refuses to
start. Signing happens after rendering and before storage.

answer:
`SignatureService` applica un sigillo PAdES usando il certificato caricato dall'HSM all'avvio; se il certificato non può essere caricato l'applicazione si rifiuta di partire [02-architecture.md — SignatureService].

La firma avviene dopo il rendering e prima dello storage [02-architecture.md — SignatureService], come conferma l'ordine del flusso: render, sigillo, upload e scrittura della riga in `documents` [05-main-flows.md — Document production flow].

question: In quali casi l'emissione di una fattura può fallire?

context.heading: GET /documents/{id}
context.content:
Returns the document request with its current status and, once rendered, the
document id and a short-lived download URL.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

context.heading: Login Flow
context.content:
1. `POST /auth/login` reaches `AuthController.login`.
2. `AuthService.authenticate` loads the account by email via `UserRepository`.
3. The password is verified against `password_hash` with argon2id.
4. On success `AuthService` issues an access token and a refresh token, and
   stores the refresh token hash through `SessionRepository.create`.

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:
Moves an invoice from `draft` to `open`, assigns the invoice `number`, renders
the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

answer:
Secondo la documentazione fornita l'emissione può fallire prima di qualsiasi addebito, in tre modi:

1. La fattura non è in stato `draft`: la rotta risponde HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue] [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
2. L'allocazione del numero va in conflitto, per violazione dell'indice unico su `invoices.number` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
3. Il render del PDF fallisce e il job viene ritentato dal worker [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].

In tutti i casi un'emissione fallita lascia la fattura in `draft` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures]. Il passaggio di stato e l'assegnazione del numero avvengono in `InvoiceService.issue`, prima che venga messo in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].

question: Qual è la differenza tra InvoiceService e PaymentService?

`PaymentService` executes charges and refunds. `StripeGateway` is the only
component that performs HTTP calls to Stripe. `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe
callbacks. `SubscriptionRepository`, `InvoiceRepository` and `PaymentRepository`
own database access.

context.content:

mark an invoice as uncollectible. It depends on `StripeGateway` for the actual
call and on `PaymentRepository` to record each attempt. Retry state lives in the
`payment_attempts` table, not in memory.

`DATABASE_URL` is the Postgres connection string. `DB_POOL_SIZE` defaults to 10
connections per replica. `DB_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS` defaults to 5000 and is

Configuration is read at boot by `config/loadConfig.ts`. Values come from

Solo in base al codice di errore riportato dal provider.

question: Perché ogni consumer della coda deve essere idempotente?

context.heading: Deployment
context.content:
The service runs as two workloads from the same image: the HTTP API and the
`billing-worker` process that drains the job queue. Both are deployed together
and share the same configuration.

context.heading: Queue
context.content:
Long running work is pushed to Redis and consumed by `billing-worker`. Invoice
issuing, dunning emails and webhook replays are queued. The queue is at-least
once: every consumer must be idempotent.

answer:

Il lavoro lungo viene spinto su Redis e consumato da `billing-worker`; in coda finiscono l'emissione delle fatture, le email di dunning e i replay dei webhook [02-architecture.md — Queue]. `billing-worker` è uno dei due workload avviati dalla stessa immagine, insieme all'API HTTP, e condivide la stessa configurazione [01-overview.md — Deployment].

question: Il provider non viene mai chiamato. Perché?

context.heading: Channel routing
context.content:
`docsync.channels` maps a channel name to a provider bean name, for example
`email: emailDeliveryProvider`. A channel absent from this map is unsupported at
runtime.

context.heading: A provider was never called
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` rejects a delivery before calling any provider when the channel
has no mapping in `docsync.channels`. In that case the delivery is recorded with
`unsupported_channel` and no `provider_message_id` is present.

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

answer:
La causa documentata è il routing del canale.

`ProviderRouter` rifiuta la delivery prima di chiamare qualsiasi provider quando il canale non ha una mappatura in `docsync.channels`; in quel caso la delivery viene registrata con `unsupported_channel` e non è presente nessun `provider_message_id` [08-troubleshooting.md — A provider was never called].

Coerentemente, se il canale non ha mappatura la delivery viene rifiutata subito con `unsupported_channel` e nessun provider viene chiamato [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter]. La mappatura è `docsync.channels`, che associa un nome di canale a un bean provider, ad esempio `email: emailDeliveryProvider`; un canale assente dalla mappa è non supportato a runtime [06-configuration.md — Channel routing].

Da verificare: il valore del campo `channel` della richiesta e la presenza della chiave corrispondente in `docsync.channels`. La tabella di routing è costruita all'avvio dalla configurazione, quindi una modifica non applicata a runtime è un'ipotesi coerente ma non confermata dalle sezioni fornite [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter].

question: Dove finisce il PDF dopo essere stato generato?

context.heading: Storage
context.content:
Rendered documents are stored in S3 under `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`.
`StorageService` is the only component that touches the S3 client. Object keys
are never reused; a re-render produces a new document id.

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.heading: documents
context.content:
`documents` holds `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`,
`signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`. One row per successfully rendered
artefact.

context.heading: Document production flow
context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
`{ "error": "<code>", "requestId": "<id>" }`. The `requestId` matches the
`X-Request-Id` header and is the key to correlate gateway and upstream logs.

context.heading: Authorisation errors
context.content:
`insufficient_scope` (HTTP 403) is returned when a route requires a scope the
token does not carry, for example calling `GET /users/:id` without
`users:read`.

context.heading: Position in the platform
context.content:
Clients talk only to the gateway. Internal services are not reachable from
outside the cluster. The gateway adds the `X-Request-Id` and `X-Caller-Id`
headers that downstream services log and propagate.

answer:
Finisce su S3, sotto la chiave `documents/{tenantId}/{documentId}.pdf`, e solo `StorageService` tocca il client S3 [02-architecture.md — Storage].

Nel flusso, dopo il render il PDF viene sigillato da `SignatureService` e poi caricato da `StorageService`, che scrive la riga in `documents` [05-main-flows.md — Document production flow]. La riga contiene `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`, `signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at` [03-data-model.md — documents].

Le chiavi degli oggetti non vengono mai riusate: un nuovo render produce un nuovo document id [02-architecture.md — Storage].

question: Cosa succede dalla chiamata a issue fino alla fattura pagata?

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.heading: Error envelope
context.content:
Every error response uses `{ "error": "<code>", "message": "<human text>" }`.
The `error` code is stable and safe to switch on; `message` is not.

context.heading: RateLimiter
context.content:
`RateLimiter` is a token bucket keyed by caller id and route. Buckets live in
Redis so all gateway replicas share the same budget. When the bucket is empty
the request is rejected with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header.

context.heading: Client timeouts
context.content:
Clients are expected to use a timeout larger than the gateway timeout, otherwise
they will give up while the gateway is still waiting for the upstream.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

answer:
Il percorso documentato attraversa tre flussi.

1. Emissione: `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` chiama `InvoiceService.issue`, che verifica lo stato `draft`, alloca il numero con `InvoiceRepository.assign_number`, renderizza e carica il PDF salvando `pdf_url`, e mette in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].
2. Addebito: `billing-worker` prende il job e chiama `PaymentService.charge`, che carica fattura e tentativi precedenti, chiama `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` con una idempotency key derivata da `invoice_id` e `attempt_number`, e scrive la riga in `payment_attempts` prima che la chiamata ritorni [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow] [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow].
3. Conferma: Stripe conferma in modo asincrono; l'evento arriva su `POST /webhooks/stripe`, viene inserito in `webhook_events` e messo in coda come `process_event`. Il worker mappa `payment_intent.succeeded` sullo stato `paid` della fattura e `payment_intent.payment_failed` su una nuova decisione di retry [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow] [05-main-flows.md — Webhook flow].

question: L'utente non riceve il documento. Da dove parto?

context.heading: deliveries

context.content:

document id and a short-lived download URL.

`rendered` but there is no delivery row, the delivery step was never invoked.

status and the `errorCode` of each attempt.

context.content:

`provider`, `status`, `attemptNumber` and `errorCode`.

answer:
La documentazione descrive esattamente questo percorso di indagine.

Controllare prima lo stato della richiesta con `GET /documents/{id}` [08-troubleshooting.md — The recipient did not receive the document], che restituisce lo stato corrente e, una volta renderizzato, l'id del documento e un URL di download a breve scadenza [04-api-reference.md — GET /documents/{id}].
2. Se lo stato è `rendered` ma non esiste nessuna riga di delivery, il passo di consegna non è mai stato invocato [08-troubleshooting.md — The recipient did not receive the document].
3. Se invece le delivery esistono, `GET /documents/{id}/deliveries` mostra provider, stato, `attemptNumber` e `errorCode` di ogni tentativo, dal più recente [04-api-reference.md — GET /documents/{id}/deliveries] [08-troubleshooting.md — The recipient did not receive the document].

question: Cosa succede dalla chiamata a issue fino alla fattura pagata?

context.heading: Charge flow
context.content:
1. `PaymentService.charge` loads the invoice and the previous attempts.
2. `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` is called with an idempotency key
   derived from `invoice_id` and `attempt_number`.
3. The attempt row is written to `payment_attempts` before the call returns.
4. Stripe confirms asynchronously; the outcome arrives via webhook.

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

answer:
Il percorso documentato attraversa tre flussi.

1. Emissione: `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` chiama `InvoiceService.issue`, che verifica lo stato `draft`, alloca il numero con `InvoiceRepository.assign_number`, renderizza e carica il PDF salvando `pdf_url`, e mette in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].
2. Addebito: `billing-worker` prende il job e chiama `PaymentService.charge`, che carica fattura e tentativi precedenti, chiama `StripeGateway.create_payment_intent` con una idempotency key derivata da `invoice_id` e `attempt_number`, e scrive la riga in `payment_attempts` prima che la chiamata ritorni [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow] [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow].
3. Conferma: Stripe conferma in modo asincrono; l'evento arriva su `POST /webhooks/stripe`, viene inserito in `webhook_events` e messo in coda come `process_event`. Il worker mappa `payment_intent.succeeded` sullo stato `paid` della fattura e `payment_intent.payment_failed` su una nuova decisione di retry [05-main-flows.md — Charge flow] [05-main-flows.md — Webhook flow].

question: Quali errori del provider fanno scattare un retry?

context.heading: Authorisation errors
context.content:
`insufficient_scope` (HTTP 403) is returned when a route requires a scope the
token does not carry, for example calling `GET /users/:id` without
`users:read`.

context.heading: Provider errors
context.content:
`StripeGateway` translates provider failures into `ProviderCardError`,
`ProviderRateLimited` and `ProviderUnavailable`. `ProviderCardError` is final:
the attempt is recorded and no retry is scheduled. `ProviderRateLimited` and
`ProviderUnavailable` are retryable and consume one of the
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` attempts.

context.heading: Documents are produced but not signed
context.content:
`documents.signed` is false only if the signing step was skipped, which happens
when the request was replayed from a pre-signature checkpoint. The HSM
certificate itself cannot be missing at runtime, because the application fails
to start without it.

context.heading: Purpose
context.content:
DocSync generates, signs and delivers documents (contracts, certificates,
policy files) to end users. It is a Java 21 Spring Boot service. Documents are
produced from templates, stored in object storage and delivered through one of
several delivery providers.

context.heading: documents
context.content:
`documents` holds `id`, `request_id`, `storage_key`, `checksum_sha256`,
`signed`, `size_bytes`, `created_at`. One row per successfully rendered
artefact.

context.heading: Retry settings
context.content:
`PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` defaults to 4. `PAYMENT_RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS` defaults to
`[1, 24, 72]`, so the second attempt happens one hour after the first, the third
a day later and the fourth three days later.

answer:
Sono retryable `ProviderRateLimited` e `ProviderUnavailable`, e ciascun tentativo consuma uno dei `PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` [07-errors.md — Provider errors].

`ProviderCardError` invece è definitivo: il tentativo viene registrato e non viene pianificato nessun retry [07-errors.md — Provider errors].

I parametri sono `PAYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` (default 4) e `PAYMENT_RETRY_BACKOFF_HOURS` (default `[1, 24, 72]`), quindi il secondo tentativo avviene un'ora dopo il primo, il terzo un giorno dopo e il quarto tre giorni dopo [06-configuration.md — Retry settings].

question: In quali casi l'emissione di una fattura può fallire?

context.heading: Issuing failures
context.content:
Issuing can fail before any charge: the invoice is not in `draft` state, the
number allocation conflicts (unique violation on `invoices.number`), or the PDF
render step fails and the job is retried by the worker. A failed issue leaves
the invoice in `draft`.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:
Moves an invoice from `draft` to `open`, assigns the invoice `number`, renders
the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

context.heading: Invoice issuing flow
context.content:
1. `POST /invoices/{id}/issue` reaches `InvoiceService.issue`.
2. The invoice status is checked; only `draft` can be issued.
3. `InvoiceRepository.assign_number` allocates the next invoice number.
4. The PDF is rendered and uploaded; `pdf_url` is stored.
5. A `charge_invoice` job is pushed to the queue.
6. `billing-worker` picks up the job and calls `PaymentService.charge`.

answer:
Secondo la documentazione fornita l'emissione può fallire prima di qualsiasi addebito, in tre modi:

1. La fattura non è in stato `draft`: la rotta risponde HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices/{id}/issue] [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
2. L'allocazione del numero va in conflitto, per violazione dell'indice unico su `invoices.number` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].
3. Il render del PDF fallisce e il job viene ritentato dal worker [07-errors.md — Issuing failures].

In tutti i casi un'emissione fallita lascia la fattura in `draft` [07-errors.md — Issuing failures]. Il passaggio di stato e l'assegnazione del numero avvengono in `InvoiceService.issue`, prima che venga messo in coda il job `charge_invoice` [05-main-flows.md — Invoice issuing flow].

question: Qual è il ruolo di UserService?

context.heading: Layers
context.content:
Requests enter through `AuthController` or `UserController`. Controllers do no
business logic: they validate the request shape and delegate to a service.
Services (`AuthService`, `UserService`, `ProfileService`) hold the business
rules. Repositories (`UserRepository`, `ProfileRepository`, `SessionRepository`)
are the only code allowed to talk to the database.

context.heading: UserService
context.content:

composes the account record and the profile record into the `CurrentUser`
object returned by the API. It depends on `UserRepository` for the account row
and on `ProfileService` for profile fields. `UserService` never queries the
database directly.

context.heading: Upstream errors
context.content:
`upstream_timeout` (HTTP 504) when the upstream exceeds the route timeout.
`upstream_unavailable` (HTTP 502) when the connection fails. The gateway never
converts an upstream 5xx into a 2xx: upstream status codes above 499 are passed
through unchanged, with the body replaced by the gateway error envelope.

context.heading: subscriptions
context.content:

`current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`. `status` is one of `trialing`,
`active`, `past_due`, `canceled`.

context.heading: POST /invoices/{id}/issue
context.content:

the PDF and enqueues the first payment attempt. Returns HTTP 202. Issuing is
rejected with HTTP 409 `invoice_not_draft` if the invoice is not in `draft`.

`UserService` è il punto di ingresso per tutto ciò che riguarda un account utente: compone il record di account e il record di profilo nell'oggetto `CurrentUser` restituito dall'API [02-architecture.md — UserService].

Dipende da `UserRepository` per la riga di account e da `ProfileService` per i campi di profilo, e non interroga mai direttamente il database [02-architecture.md — UserService]. question: Come viene garantita l'idempotenza dei webhook?

context.heading: Webhook failures
context.content:
A webhook with an invalid signature is rejected with HTTP 400
`invalid_signature` and is not stored. A webhook whose `provider_event_id` is
already present is acknowledged with HTTP 200 and dropped.

context.heading: webhook_events
context.content:
`webhook_events` stores every received Stripe event with `provider_event_id`
(unique), `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`. The unique index on
`provider_event_id` is what makes webhook processing idempotent.

context.heading: Webhook flow
context.content:
1. Stripe posts to `POST /webhooks/stripe`.
2. `WebhookHandler.receive` verifies the signature and inserts into
   `webhook_events`; a duplicate `provider_event_id` is ignored.
3. A `process_event` job is queued.
4. `billing-worker` maps `payment_intent.succeeded` to invoice `paid` and
   `payment_intent.payment_failed` to a new retry decision.

answer:
Tramite l'indice unico su `provider_event_id` nella tabella `webhook_events`.

- Ogni evento Stripe ricevuto viene salvato in `webhook_events` con `provider_event_id` unico, `type`, `payload`, `processed_at`; è proprio quell'indice unico a rendere idempotente l'elaborazione [03-data-model.md — webhook_events].
- `WebhookHandler.receive` verifica la firma e inserisce l'evento; un `provider_event_id` duplicato viene ignorato [05-main-flows.md — Webhook flow].
- Un webhook già presente viene comunque confermato con HTTP 200 e scartato [07-errors.md — Webhook failures].

context.content:

2. `authMiddleware` verifies the token and sets `req.auth.userId`.
3. `UserController.getMe` calls `UserService.getCurrentUser(userId)`.
4. `UserService` loads the account through `UserRepository.findById`.
5. `UserService` loads profile fields through `ProfileService.getProfile`.
6. The two records are merged into `CurrentUser` and serialised.

`displayName` falls back to the email local part.

context.heading: PaymentService
context.content:
`PaymentService` decides when to charge, how many times to retry and when to
mark an invoice as uncollectible. It depends on `StripeGateway` for the actual
call and on `PaymentRepository` to record each attempt. Retry state lives in the
`payment_attempts` table, not in memory.

context.content:
1. `POST /documents` stores a `document_requests` row with status `received`.
2. The request is queued; a worker moves it to `rendering`.
3. `RenderService` resolves the active template and renders the PDF.
4. `SignatureService` seals the PDF.
5. `StorageService` uploads it and writes the `documents` row.
6. The request moves to `rendered`.

is unknown, expired or already revoked, the route returns HTTP 401 with
`{ "error": "invalid_refresh_token" }`.

context.content:

retries idempotent methods and records the upstream latency metric
`gateway_upstream_duration_seconds`.

context.content:

`PaymentService` executes charges and refunds. `StripeGateway` is the only
component that performs HTTP calls to Stripe. `WebhookHandler` consumes Stripe
callbacks. `SubscriptionRepository`, `InvoiceRepository` and `PaymentRepository`

question: Qual è lo SLA di disponibilità per Channel routing?

question: Qual è il ruolo di DeliveryService?

context.heading: Access tokens
context.content:
Access tokens are short lived. The platform standard is a 60 minute access
token lifetime, and Acme Identity follows the platform standard.

context.heading: sessions table
context.content:
The `sessions` table holds refresh tokens: `id`, `user_id`, `refresh_token_hash`,
`user_agent`, `expires_at`, `revoked_at`. Access tokens are never stored; only
refresh tokens are persisted, and only as a hash.

context.heading: DeliveryService
context.content:
`DeliveryService` selects a provider for each delivery and calls it through the
`DeliveryProvider` interface. Implementations are `EmailDeliveryProvider`,
`PecDeliveryProvider` and `PortalDeliveryProvider`. Selection is driven by the
`channel` field of the request, resolved by `ProviderRouter`.

context.heading: POST /auth/refresh
context.content:
Accepts `{ refreshToken }` and returns a new access token. If the refresh token
is unknown, expired or already revoked, the route returns HTTP 401 with
`{ "error": "invalid_refresh_token" }`.

context.heading: ProviderRouter
context.content:
`ProviderRouter` maps a channel to a provider bean. If the channel has no
mapping the delivery is rejected immediately with `unsupported_channel` and no
provider is called. The routing table is built at startup from configuration.

answer:
`DeliveryService` sceglie un provider per ogni delivery e lo chiama attraverso l'interfaccia `DeliveryProvider` [02-architecture.md — DeliveryService].

Le implementazioni documentate sono `EmailDeliveryProvider`, `PecDeliveryProvider` e `PortalDeliveryProvider`, e la selezione è guidata dal campo `channel` della richiesta, risolto da `ProviderRouter` [02-architecture.md — DeliveryService]. `ProviderRouter` costruisce la tabella di routing all'avvio dalla configurazione [02-architecture.md — ProviderRouter].

question: Quando una consegna viene ritentata?

context.heading: deliveries
context.content:
`deliveries` holds `id`, `document_id`, `provider`, `recipient`, `status`,
`provider_message_id`, `error_code`, `attempt_number`, `created_at`,
`updated_at`. `status` is one of `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`,
`bounced`.

context.heading: Delivery errors
context.content:
Provider errors are normalised to `provider_rejected`, `provider_unavailable`
and `recipient_invalid`. `recipient_invalid` is final. `provider_unavailable` is
retryable. `provider_rejected` is retryable only when the provider marks the
error code as retryable.

context.heading: Retry flow
context.content:
A delivery in `rejected` state is retried only if the provider reported a
retryable error code. Retries create a new `deliveries` row with an incremented
`attempt_number`. A `bounced` delivery is never retried.

answer:
Solo in base al codice di errore riportato dal provider.

- Una delivery in stato `rejected` viene ritentata soltanto se il provider ha riportato un codice di errore retryable; i retry creano una nuova riga in `deliveries` con `attempt_number` incrementato [05-main-flows.md — Retry flow].
- Una delivery `bounced` non viene mai ritentata [05-main-flows.md — Retry flow].
- Sul lato errori: `recipient_invalid` è definitivo, `provider_unavailable` è retryable e `provider_rejected` è retryable solo quando il provider marca il codice come retryable [07-errors.md — Delivery errors].

Gli stati possibili di una delivery sono `queued`, `sent`, `accepted`, `rejected`, `bounced` [03-data-model.md — deliveries].

question: Che differenza c'è tra la tabella users e la tabella user_profiles?

context.heading: users table
context.content:
The `users` table holds the account record: `id` (uuid, primary key), `email`,
`password_hash`, `status`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. The `email` column has a
unique index. `status` is one of `active`, `pending`, `suspended`.

context.heading: user_profiles table
context.content:
The `user_profiles` table holds profile data: `user_id` (uuid, primary key and
foreign key to `users.id`), `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone`,
`updated_at`. There is exactly one profile row per account, created lazily on
first profile write.

answer:
Separano account e profilo.

- `users` è il record di account: `id` (uuid, chiave primaria), `email` (indice unico), `password_hash`, `status` (`active`, `pending`, `suspended`), `created_at`, `updated_at` [03-data-model.md — users table].
- `user_profiles` è il record di profilo: `user_id` come chiave primaria e foreign key verso `users.id`, più `display_name`, `avatar_url`, `locale`, `timezone`, `updated_at` [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

La relazione è uno a uno, ma la riga di profilo viene creata in modo lazy alla prima scrittura, quindi un account può esistere senza la riga corrispondente in `user_profiles` [03-data-model.md — user_profiles table].

Returns HTTP 201 with the invoice in `draft` status. Creating an invoice does
not charge anything.

context.content:
`validation_failed` (HTTP 422) is returned when the request body does not match

No. `POST /invoices` crea una fattura in stato `draft` e restituisce HTTP 201; la creazione non addebita nulla [04-api-reference.md — POST /invoices].
